Getting started with vaxsurvR

Source: vignettes/vaxsurvR.Rmd
vaxsurvR.Rmd
library(vaxsurvR)

What the package is for

A vaccination coverage survey arrives as a wide export from a mobile data-collection platform: one row per interview, repeat groups flattened into column names, everything stored as text, and a vaccination card transcribed into dozens of status and date columns per child.

Getting from that to a defensible coverage estimate involves a long series of decisions – which variable means what, which dates are usable, what counts as a vaccinated child, whose weight applies. vaxsurvR makes each of those decisions an explicit, testable function call rather than a line buried in a cleaning script.

The object you work with

vcs_data holds three standardised tables plus the untouched import.

vcs_example
#> <vcs_data>
#>   households  : 600
#>   children    : 256
#>   vaccinations: 3584 rows (14 vaccine[s])
#>   source      : synthetic (data-raw/make_vcs_example.R)
summary(vcs_example)
#> <vcs_data summary>
#>   households   600
#>   children     256
#>   psus         30
#>   segments     2
#>   strata       2
#>   vaccines     14
#>   card seen    58.2%
#>   card doses   64.5%
#>   dated doses  86.3%
  • $households – one row per interview
  • $children – one row per eligible child
  • $vaccinations – one row per child-vaccine combination, in long form
  • $raw – the import, never modified
head(vcs_example$children[, c("child_id", "interview_id", "sex", "card_seen")])
#> # A tibble: 6 × 4
#>   child_id interview_id sex   card_seen
#>   <chr>    <chr>        <chr> <lgl>    
#> 1 CH00021  uuid:HH0002  2     TRUE     
#> 2 CH00031  uuid:HH0003  1     TRUE     
#> 3 CH00041  uuid:HH0004  2     TRUE     
#> 4 CH00051  uuid:HH0005  1     TRUE     
#> 5 CH00121  uuid:HH0012  2     TRUE     
#> 6 CH00141  uuid:HH0014  1     FALSE
head(vcs_example$vaccinations[, c("child_id", "vaccine", "card_status", "card_date")])
#> # A tibble: 6 × 4
#>   child_id vaccine card_status card_date 
#>   <chr>    <chr>   <chr>       <date>    
#> 1 CH00021  BCG     1           2025-02-05
#> 2 CH00031  BCG     1           2024-05-29
#> 3 CH00041  BCG     2           NA        
#> 4 CH00051  BCG     1           2025-05-01
#> 5 CH00121  BCG     1           2024-05-14
#> 6 CH00141  BCG     98          NA

Observed and derived variables stay apart

Any column the package computes carries the rule that produced it.

derivation_rules(vcs_example)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>   table        variable        rule                                             
#>   <chr>        <chr>           <chr>                                            
#> 1 vaccinations card_documented card_status in {1, 2} = documented, in {0, 3, no…
#> 2 vaccinations recall_reported recall_reported from recall_status per dose; don…

A first pass

Validate, then look at what came back. Checks return objects, not messages.

qa <- validate_vcs(vcs_example)
qa
#> <vcs_validation: 15 check(s), 811 issue(s)>
#>   INFO: 103  WARNING: 302  ERROR: 350  CRITICAL: 56
#> 
#>   [CRITICAL] ID_DUPLICATE CH02731: Identifier "child_id" is not unique.
#>   [CRITICAL] ID_DUPLICATE CH02731: Identifier "child_id" is not unique.
#>   [CRITICAL] DATE_PREBIRTH CH00121/BCG: Vaccination recorded 4 day(s) before the date of birth.
#>   [CRITICAL] DATE_PREBIRTH CH00181/BCG: Vaccination recorded 1 day(s) before the date of birth.
#>   [CRITICAL] DATE_PREBIRTH CH00301/BCG: Vaccination recorded 2 day(s) before the date of birth.
#>   [CRITICAL] DATE_PREBIRTH CH00531/BCG: Vaccination recorded 6 day(s) before the date of birth.
#>   [CRITICAL] DATE_PREBIRTH CH01321/BCG: Vaccination recorded 9 day(s) before the date of birth.
#>   [CRITICAL] DATE_PREBIRTH CH01591/BCG: Vaccination recorded 7 day(s) before the date of birth.
#>   [CRITICAL] DATE_PREBIRTH CH01691/BCG: Vaccination recorded 23 day(s) before the date of birth.
#>   [CRITICAL] DATE_PREBIRTH CH01701/BCG: Vaccination recorded 4 day(s) before the date of birth.
#>   ... and 801 more; use issues() for the full table
summary(qa, by = "severity")
#> # A tibble: 4 × 4
#>   group    severity n_issues n_records
#>   <chr>    <chr>       <int>     <int>
#> 1 CRITICAL CRITICAL       56        55
#> 2 ERROR    ERROR         350       304
#> 3 WARNING  WARNING       302       198
#> 4 INFO     INFO          103       103
head(issues(qa, severity = "CRITICAL"))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 8
#>   check                  rule_id severity level record_id variable value message
#>   <chr>                  <chr>   <fct>    <chr> <chr>     <chr>    <chr> <chr>  
#> 1 check_unique_ids       ID_DUP… CRITICAL child CH02731   child_id CH02… "Ident…
#> 2 check_unique_ids       ID_DUP… CRITICAL child CH02731   child_id CH02… "Ident…
#> 3 check_prebirth_vaccin… DATE_P… CRITICAL vacc… CH00121/… card_da… 2024… "Vacci…
#> 4 check_prebirth_vaccin… DATE_P… CRITICAL vacc… CH00181/… card_da… 2024… "Vacci…
#> 5 check_prebirth_vaccin… DATE_P… CRITICAL vacc… CH00301/… card_da… 2024… "Vacci…
#> 6 check_prebirth_vaccin… DATE_P… CRITICAL vacc… CH00531/… card_da… 2024… "Vacci…

A first estimate

Derive a coverage indicator, build the design, estimate.

d   <- derive_vaccination_status(vcs_example, evidence = "card_or_recall")
des <- vcs_design(d)
des
#> <vcs_design>
#>   records : 256
#>   ids     : psu + segment
#>   strata  : stratum
#>   weights : weight
#>   lonely PSU rule: adjust
estimate_coverage(des, vaccines = c("BCG", "PENTA1", "PENTA3", "MCV1"))
#> <vcs_estimate: 4 row(s)>
#>   evidence : card_or_recall
#> # A tibble: 4 × 13
#>   indicator domain    numerator denominator estimate     se conf_low conf_high
#>   <chr>     <chr>         <dbl>       <dbl>    <dbl>  <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 BCG       <overall>       218         253    0.852 0.0235    0.806     0.898
#> 2 PENTA1    <overall>       227         252    0.907 0.0155    0.876     0.937
#> 3 PENTA3    <overall>       137         255    0.543 0.0302    0.484     0.602
#> 4 MCV1      <overall>       151         253    0.608 0.0320    0.545     0.671
#> # ℹ 5 more variables: n_unweighted <dbl>, deff <dbl>, neff <dbl>, icc <dbl>,
#> #   ci_method <chr>

Coverage falls along the schedule, which is what dropout measures:

estimate_dropout(des, first = "PENTA1", last = "PENTA3")
#> <vcs_estimate: 1 row(s)>
#> # A tibble: 1 × 14
#>   indicator      domain numerator denominator estimate     se conf_low conf_high
#>   <chr>          <chr>      <dbl>       <dbl>    <dbl>  <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 PENTA1-PENTA3… <over…        94         226    0.415 0.0291    0.358     0.472
#> # ℹ 6 more variables: n_unweighted <dbl>, deff <dbl>, neff <dbl>, icc <dbl>,
#> #   ci_method <chr>, method <chr>
